require 'webrick'
require 'json'
require 'thread'

module RateLimiter
  WINDOW_SIZE = 60
  MAX_REQUESTS = 100

  class TokenBucket
    attr_reader :tokens, :capacity

    def initialize(capacity, refill_rate)
      @capacity = capacity
      @tokens = capacity
      @refill_rate = refill_rate
      @last_refill = Process.clock_gettime(Process::CLOCK_MONOTONIC)
      @mutex = Mutex.new
    end

    def consume(count = 1)
      @mutex.synchronize do
        refill
        if @tokens >= count
          @tokens -= count
          true
        else
          false
        end
      end
    end

    def remaining
      @mutex.synchronize { @tokens }
    end

    private

    def refill
      now = Process.clock_gettime(Process::CLOCK_MONOTONIC)
      elapsed = now - @last_refill
      new_tokens = (elapsed * @refill_rate).to_i
      if new_tokens > 0
        @tokens = [@tokens + new_tokens, @capacity].min
        @last_refill = now
      end
    end
  end
end

module ConnectionPool
  class Pool
    def initialize(max_size)
      @max_size = max_size
      @active_connections = 0
      @pending_requests = 0
      @mutex = Mutex.new
      @drain_condition = ConditionVariable.new
      @draining = false
    end

    def acquire
      @mutex.synchronize do
        return nil if @draining && @active_connections >= @max_size
        @active_connections += 1
        @pending_requests += 1
      end
      true
    end

    def release
      @mutex.synchronize do
        @active_connections -= 1
        @pending_requests -= 1
        @drain_condition.signal if @draining && @active_connections == 0
      end
    end

    def drain(timeout = 30)
      deadline = Process.clock_gettime(Process::CLOCK_MONOTONIC) + timeout
      @mutex.synchronize do
        @draining = true
        while @active_connections > 0
          remaining = deadline - Process.clock_gettime(Process::CLOCK_MONOTONIC)
          break if remaining <= 0
          @drain_condition.wait(@mutex, remaining)
        end
      end
    end

    def compute_available_slots
      @mutex.synchronize do
        @max_size - @pending_requests
      end
    end

    def stats
      @mutex.synchronize do
        { active: @active_connections, pending: @pending_requests,
          available: compute_available_slots_unsafe, draining: @draining }
      end
    end

    private

    def compute_available_slots_unsafe
      @max_size - @pending_requests
    end
  end
end

class MicroService
  MAX_BATCH_COUNT = 1000
  MIN_BATCH_COUNT = 1

  def initialize(port: 8080, max_connections: 50)
    @port = port
    @pool = ConnectionPool::Pool.new(max_connections)
    @limiter = RateLimiter::TokenBucket.new(RateLimiter::MAX_REQUESTS, 2)
    @shutdown_hooks = []
    @request_counter = 0
    @counter_mutex = Mutex.new
    setup_signal_handlers
  end

  def start
    @server = WEBrick::HTTPServer.new(Port: @port, Logger: WEBrick::Log.new("/dev/null"))
    mount_endpoints
    @server.start
  end

  private

  def setup_signal_handlers
    %w[INT TERM].each do |sig|
      Signal.trap(sig) { graceful_shutdown }
    end
  end

  def graceful_shutdown
    Thread.new do
      @pool.drain(30)
      @shutdown_hooks.each(&:call)
      @server&.shutdown
    end
  end

  def mount_endpoints
    @server.mount_proc '/api/allocate' do |req, res|
      handle_allocate(req, res)
    end

    @server.mount_proc '/api/stats' do |req, res|
      handle_stats(req, res)
    end

    @server.mount_proc '/api/batch' do |req, res|
      handle_batch(req, res)
    end
  end

  def handle_allocate(req, res)
    unless @limiter.consume
      res.status = 429
      res.body = JSON.generate({ error: 'rate limited' })
      return
    end

    unless @pool.acquire
      res.status = 503
      res.body = JSON.generate({ error: 'service unavailable' })
      return
    end

    begin
      slots = @pool.compute_available_slots
      allocation = compute_allocation(req, slots)
      res.status = 200
      res.body = JSON.generate({ allocated: allocation, remaining_slots: slots })
    ensure
      @pool.release
    end
  end

  def handle_batch(req, res)
    unless @limiter.consume
      res.status = 429
      res.body = JSON.generate({ error: 'rate limited' })
      return
    end

    body = JSON.parse(req.body || '{}')
    requested_count = (body['count'] || 1).to_i
    priority_offset = (body['priority'] || 0).to_i

    effective_count = apply_priority_adjustment(requested_count, priority_offset)

    unless @pool.acquire
      res.status = 503
      res.body = JSON.generate({ error: 'service unavailable' })
      return
    end

    begin
      results = process_batch(effective_count)
      res.status = 200
      res.body = JSON.generate({ results: results, processed: effective_count })
    ensure
      @pool.release
    end
  end

  def apply_priority_adjustment(count, priority)
    # Priority levels: -5 (lowest) to +5 (highest)
    # Higher priority gets more allocation, lower gets reduced
    # Clamp priority to valid range
    priority = [[-5, priority].max, 5].min
    count = [[MIN_BATCH_COUNT, count].max, MAX_BATCH_COUNT].min
    adjustment = priority * (count / 10)
    result = count + adjustment
    # Ensure result is always within safe bounds
    [[MIN_BATCH_COUNT, result].max, MAX_BATCH_COUNT].min
  end

  def process_batch(count)
    # Allocate buffer based on computed count
    buffer_size = count * 64
    Array.new(buffer_size, 0).each_slice(64).map do |chunk|
      { processed: true, size: chunk.length }
    end
  end

  def compute_allocation(req, available_slots)
    params = req.query
    requested = (params['size'] || '1').to_i
    [requested, [available_slots, 0].max].min
  end

  def handle_stats(req, res)
    stats = @pool.stats
    stats[:rate_limiter_remaining] = @limiter.remaining
    res.status = 200
    res.body = JSON.generate(stats)
  end
end

if __FILE__ == $0
  service = MicroService.new(port: ENV.fetch('PORT', 8080).to_i)
  service.start
end
